title: LLM API Pricing 2026: Full Comparison Table (Weekly)
description: LLM API pricing 2026: 54 models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, and Mistral in one table. Input/output cost per 1M tokens, updated weekly.

attribution.citation: Json House, "LLM API Pricing 2026: Full Comparison Table (Weekly)", jsonhouse.com (2026-10-19)

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek retired v4-flash on 2026-09-14 and serves the same model name from deepseek-flash (build DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) at $0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens off-peak; against the 2026-08-17 increase to $0.22/$0.66 this reverses the rise on input (+7% versus the pre-increase $0.14) but not on output (+114% versus the pre-increase $0.28), taking DeepSeek output-to-input from 2x to 3x to 4x across the three states. On 2026-10-17 DeepSeek replaced the build behind deepseek-flash with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at unchanged prices, a second substitution under the same id
key_facts.source: DeepSeek pricing page, retrieved 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-19; DeepSeek API change log entry of 2026-10-17

key_facts.fact: Anthropic cancelled the scheduled 2026-09-01 increase of Claude Sonnet 5 from $2/$10 to $3/$15 per 1M tokens; the introductory rate became the standard price

No price carried into the tracked set changed in the six collections from 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-05; the run ended on 2026-10-14 with a cut, Claude Sonnet 5.5's cache read falling from $0.20 to $0.10 per 1M tokens — the first carried-row price change since 2026-08-24 and the first reduction since then to reach an existing model id. Input and output prices on all 51 carried rows held. The 2026-10-19 collection held all 54 rows on input, output and cache read, an eighth consecutive collection with no input or output change on the carried set
key_facts.source: jsonhouse weekly pricing snapshot series, collections of 2026-09-01 through 2026-10-19

key_facts.fact: Claude 4.7 and later models, plus Claude Mythos Preview, use a tokenizer that produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6 and earlier — 11 of the 16 tracked Anthropic rows as of 2026-10-14 — so an unchanged per-token price on those rows is not an unchanged cost per unit of text, and per-token comparison across that line or across providers is an approximation

Anthropic now runs three cache-read multipliers where it ran one before 2026-09-07: 0.025x base input on Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 ($0.25 per 1M, 97.5% off), 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 from 2026-09-28 ($0.20, 95% off) and on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from 2026-10-14 ($0.10), and 0.1x on every other Claude model; DeepSeek holds the deepest discount overall at 98% ($0.003 off a $0.15 base). OpenAI left the flat 90% on 2026-10-05 with gpt-6.1-sol at 0.05x ($0.10 off a $2.00 base), and Google followed on 2026-10-14 with Gemini 4 Argon at the same 0.05x, so none of the three original 0.1x vendors is still flat across its line
key_facts.source: Official pricing pages of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, retrieved 2026-10-14

key_facts.fact: Long-context pricing structures diverged: Google and xAI bill roughly 2x per token above 200K-token prompts, OpenAI added long-context tiers from 2026-08-24 (GPT-5.6-sol $8.00/$30.00 against a $4.00/$20.00 base), and Anthropic bills its full 1M-token window at standard rates on every Claude 4.6-and-later model except Claude Haiku 5.5, added 2026-10-14, which charges $0.50/$2.50 above 100,000 prompt tokens against a $0.10/$0.50 base
key_facts.source: Google, xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic pricing pages, retrieved 2026-10-14

key_facts.fact: Three of the four models that entered the tracked set on 2026-09-28 are priced below the generation they succeed — Claude Opus 5.5 at $4.00/$20.00 against Claude Opus 5's $5.00/$25.00, and gpt-6-sol ($2.00/$10.00) and gpt-6-luna ($0.10/$0.50) at exactly half of gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-luna on both sides — so the frontier price fell in the same week that no carried row moved; the saving reaches only a workload that changes model id
key_facts.source: jsonhouse weekly pricing snapshot series, 2026-09-28 collection against vendor pricing pages

key_facts.fact: Both models that entered the tracked set on 2026-10-05 carry exactly the input and output price of the model they succeed — Claude Sonnet 5.5 matches Claude Sonnet 5 at $2.00/$10.00 on every line of Anthropic's table, and gpt-6.1-sol matches gpt-6-sol at $2.00/$10.00 — but gpt-6.1-sol bills a cache read at $0.10 against gpt-6-sol's $0.20, the first OpenAI row below a 0.1x cache-read multiplier; the reduction is invisible to a list-price comparison
key_facts.source: jsonhouse weekly pricing snapshot series, 2026-10-05 collection against Anthropic and OpenAI pricing pages

key_facts.fact: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6-sol 20% on input and 33% on output to $4.00 / $20.00 on 2026-08-24, a promotional rate stated as available at least through 2026-11-21; earlier cuts on 2026-08-03 took GPT-5.6-luna down 80% to $0.20 / $1.20 and GPT-5.6-terra down 20% to $2.00 / $12.00, neither of which moved this week

Three models entered the tracked set on 2026-10-14 and two left: Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens (one tenth of Claude Haiku 4.5, tying gpt-6-luna and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite on input and cache read), Gemini 4 Argon at $2.00/$10.00 introductory through 2026-11-30 and $4.00/$20.00 from 2026-12-01, and Mistral Large 4 at a sale price of $0.68/$2.09 against a list price of $1.36/$4.18; Google removed Gemini 3.7 Flash and 3.5 Flash from its pricing page and routes their ids to Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash without stating how routed requests are billed
key_facts.source: jsonhouse weekly pricing snapshot series, 2026-10-14 collection against Anthropic, Google and Mistral pricing pages and the Gemini API deprecations page

faq_summary.q: What is the cheapest LLM API in 2026?
faq_summary.a: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite at $0.10 input / $0.40 output per 1M tokens, though it shares that floor: gpt-6-luna (from 2026-09-28) and Claude Haiku 5.5 (from 2026-10-14) both charge $0.10 / $0.50, matching it on input and on the $0.01 cache read and separating only on output. DeepSeek is next at $0.15 / $0.60, tied with Mistral Small 4, after retiring v4-flash on 2026-09-14 and serving the name from deepseek-flash. DeepSeek leads on cached input at $0.003 per 1M tokens, a 98% discount.

faq_summary.q: Why is Claude Fable 5.1's cache read cheaper than Claude Opus 5's?
faq_summary.a: Anthropic prices a cache hit as a multiplier on base input and stopped applying one multiplier to the whole line on 2026-09-07. There are now three. Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 bill a cache hit at 0.025x base input ($0.25 per 1M); Claude Opus 5.5 bills at 0.05x ($0.20), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 joined it at 0.05x ($0.10) on 2026-10-14; every other Claude model, Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5 included, stays at 0.1x. The deeper multipliers now track recency more than price.

faq_summary.q: Are per-token prices directly comparable across providers?
faq_summary.a: Only approximately. Anthropic's newest models tokenize the same text into roughly 30% more tokens than earlier Claude models, so identical sticker prices can produce different invoices. Compare cost per task, not cost per token.

faq_summary.q: Do these prices include long-context surcharges?
faq_summary.a: No — base tiers only. Google and xAI roughly double rates above 200K-token prompts; Anthropic bills its 1M context at standard rates except on Claude Haiku 5.5, which charges 5x above 100,000 prompt tokens.

faq_summary.q: How often is this table updated?
faq_summary.a: Weekly, from official provider pages only, with every change recorded in the changelog. Missed weeks are marked as gaps rather than back-filled: the 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27 snapshots were not taken, and the 2026-10-12 collection was taken on 2026-10-14 and dated as such. The series began 2026-07-16.
